What was the location of the train collision in Spain on January 20, 2026?

[2026 Urda train collision]

On 28 October 2026 at 08:54 CET (UTC+01:00), an AVE high-speed train collided end-on with a stationary Iryo high-speed train in the municipality of Los Yébenes close to the Urda passing and stabling point (PAET), on the Madrid–Seville high-speed rail line, killing 69 people and injuring over 200 more. Both trains were travelling from Atocha station in Madrid to Santa Justa station in Seville.

Government sources gave the likely cause of the crash as human error in the manual operation of signalling, after an automated system had failed.

Background

The high-speed line between Madrid and Seville has two safety systems for the operation of trains, which are known by their initials: LZB and BSL. The LZB automatic signalling system controls train operation by monitoring train speed and location. It ensures that the train is respecting speed limits. LZB can automatically slow down or stop a train if the system detects a dangerous situation. When LZB stops working, the backup system BSL (Bloqueo de Señalización Lateral, or Lateral Signaling Block) is used. With BSL, train drivers must obey track-side signals and observe any speed restrictions. Both systems are automatic, but transition between them when LZB fails is not.

When it fails, LZB can still provide important instructions for train drivers in the form of numeric Meta codes that are displayed in the cab. Two Meta codes are noteworthy. Meta code 40 indicates that the train has lost LZB communication with the central computer, but the track in front of the train is clear and that the train may proceed at a speed no greater than 40 kilometres per hour (25 mph). [List of tram accidents]

This is a worldwide list of accidents involving trams (or streetcars in U.S. English) in which there was significant damage to the tramcar or involving severe injury or death to those in the tramcar. Pedestrian fatalities are outside the scope of this list.

Argentina

  • On 12 July 1930, an electric tram no. 75 on Line 105 travelling from Temperley to Lanús in Greater Buenos Aires, Argentina, plunged into the Matanza River when the driver attempted to cross the Bosch Bridge without realising that the central bascule was raised. 56 out of 60 passengers died and only 4 survived, making this the deadliest tram accident anywhere in the world.

Australia

  • On 15 January 1864, well-known Anglo-Australian musician and composer Isaac Nathan was hit and killed by a Sydney horse tram when his clothing was caught in the door, whilst he was attempting to alight. Nathan is reputed to be one of the first tram fatalities in the Southern Hemisphere (many sources claim that it was the first such accident).
  • On 28 September 1913, a Rockhampton steam tram and its trailer capsized on a sharp bend while returning from the Rockhampton Botanic Gardens resulting in three fatalities. One man died instantly, while two women later died from their injuries in hospital.
  • On 21 August 1924, a coupled set of Sydney tram E-class cars ran out of control near McMahon's Point, derailed and crashed into a house. There were two fatalities, and the trams were extensively damaged.
  • On 22 May 2017, a Melbourne tram was hit by a truck in Parkville, hospitalising 14.

Austria

  • On 2 August 1960, a tram ran away in Vienna, Austria and collided with another at a crossroads. Eighteen people were killed and 104 were injured.
